fact_text: On 14 Sep 2026 the State Bank of Pakistan's monetary policy committee kept the policy rate at 11.5%, broadly in line with market expectations.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The SBP kept its medium-to-long-term inflation target and said risks had risen compared with the previous policy meeting, while noting some positive news.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: Some experts had expected a rate hike before the decision because oil-driven commodity prices were pushing inflation up; the hold surprised that expectation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The SBP raised the policy rate by 100 basis points in April 2026, when the US-Iran war had been running for roughly a month and a quarter; the interviewee called it a pre-emptive move.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: In its late-July 2026 statement the SBP said future decisions depended on the geopolitical situation, and markets had hoped for a cut at the October or December 2026 meetings.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: A roughly six-month US-Iran conflict made supply shocks visible: Saudi output fell and waterway disruption hit oil flows, so Pakistan pays higher prices and a premium on Middle East crude imports.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The interviewee said the inflation is mainly supply-driven, led by high oil prices that lift transport and food costs, so an interest-rate tool is a weaker answer to it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: Interest rates normally cool demand, but cement, fertiliser and auto sales, the consumption indicators, had already softened in July 2026 without a rate hike, which the interviewee said gave the SBP room to hold.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: Inflation had been expected to fall to single digits on a low base effect, but high oil prices drive transport and food inflation, so it could stay in double digits.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: With the policy rate and inflation both at about 11%, the real interest rate is close to zero; the interviewee noted that near-zero or negative real rates have moved inversely with the trade deficit in the past.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: SBP reserves were about $14 billion in April 2026 and had risen by about $4 billion by 14 Sep 2026, helped by the Eurobond.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: A $3 billion Eurobond was floated, which the interviewee said strengthened the external position and the SBP's reserve buffer.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The SBP's target was for reserves to reach about $21 billion by end-December 2026, a goal the interviewee said left room for the SBP to hold rates.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: External debt repayments were about $26 billion in the prior comparison period, the interviewee said, and about $21.5 billion in 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: External debt repayments for 2026 are about $21.5 billion, and the interviewee said they put little pressure on the dollar supply.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: After excluding rollover refinancing, the actual repayments for the remaining months are about $7 billion, which the interviewee used to argue the rupee stays stable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: At the post-decision briefing on 14 Sep 2026 the SBP said remittances would exceed their $44 billion target, while imports were described as running at about $5 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: Economic growth dipped in August 2026 because of strikes and other factors, and growth was expected to pick up from September 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The SBP and the government target GDP growth of 3.5% to 4.5%; the interviewee said growth of only 3% to 4% would miss target and weaken jobs creation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: Agriculture contributes about 20% to 25% of GDP, and its output has run below expectations for two to three years, so weather disruption is a key risk to growth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The interviewee's rule of thumb: each 1% rise in the policy rate has historically coincided with a 6% to 7% correction in the stock market.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: On 14 Sep 2026 the Pakistan Stock Exchange fell about 1.8% at its lowest point, before partially recovering.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: On 14 Sep 2026 the Pakistan Stock Exchange fell by about 3,000 points at its low during the afternoon.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: On 14 Sep 2026 Maple Leaf Cement fell about 4% to 5%, a bigger drop than the broad market's sell-off.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: On 14 Sep 2026 Pakistan Petroleum posted results above expectations, which the interviewee said made it a bluechip with a strong dividend.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: On 14 Sep 2026 Pakistan Petroleum announced a dividend of Rs6 per share.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst said listed cement stocks trade at attractive valuations, with the market having partly priced in the oil shock.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst said listed refinery stocks trade at attractive valuations despite the oil price uncertainty.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst said bank stocks trade at attractive valuations, in part because the feared rate hike did not happen.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst considered UBL attractive at that price level, because the feared rate hike, which would have hurt it, did not happen.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst said the market's direction and sustainability depend on where oil prices settle, and expected the market to open positive on 15 Sep 2026 with a reaction to the decision.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The SBP's language on 14 Sep 2026 was not hawkish: it was comfortable defending reserves and the PKR parity.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst ruled out rupee depreciation on 14 Sep 2026, arguing that reserves and falling debt repayments make the rupee stable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)

fact_text: The analyst said a rate hike at the SBP policy meeting in October or December 2026 cannot be ruled out if risks stay elevated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Rate at 11.5% | Impact on Pakistan Economy & PSX | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-14)
